newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower in low-volume trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower in low-volume trade.

text.p: Share prices closed lower on the Delhi bourse on lack of strong buying support as institutional investors stayed on sidelines during a day of thin trade, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 3.75 points lower at 715.99.
Traders said lack of any market-moving news and prevailing political confusion linked to a spate of legal cases involving former premier P. V. Narasimha Rao had dampened buying interest.
Brokers said volumes were restricted to select counters.

"With the absence of any worthwhile support to the capital market and a dim political scenario, it is too difficult to see a rise in the share prices," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jaimata Securities.
Local news agencies reported Indian federal police had told a court that there was ample evidence to prosecute former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a criminal forgery case.

Court officials said chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar might issue on Thursday either a summons or a warrant for Rao to appear in court at a future date to face the charges in a forgery case, filed by the CBI on September 26.
At issue is an alleged attempt in 1989 to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.
Reliance Industries eased 1.60 rupees to 191.05, while TISCO quoted 0.35 rupee lower at 172.70.
ACC lost 54.30 to 1707.95 and State Bank of India was down 11.35 rupees at 241.40 on heavy speculative selling, brokers said.
However ITC bucked the trend to quote 5.85 rupees higher at 308.80 on buying by Calcutta-based operators, they said.
